frozen_evidence_boundary: repository source/tests only; no issues/PRs before freeze
raw_signal_observation: Plugins may hide standard SwiftBar controls such as About, Run in Terminal, Disable Plugin and the SwiftBar submenu through metadata. README documents that Option+Click reveals hidden default items, and MenuBarItem records Option state when the menu opens.
material_claim: Source establishes a hidden-control recovery mechanism. It cannot establish whether ordinary users discover or understand Option+Click when a plugin hides Disable Plugin or SwiftBar controls.
required_reality_floor: R6 for discoverability/comprehension of the recovery gesture
neta_next_move: Do not add persistent recovery UI from source inspection alone. Observe a small first-use task with a plugin that hides standard controls and record whether an external user can recover them without instruction; if not, prototype the smallest visible recovery cue.
field_requirement: External person encounters a plugin with hidden standard items and is asked to disable/reach SwiftBar controls without being told about Option+Click.
reversal_condition: If external users reliably recover the hidden controls unaided, keep the current mechanism; repeated failure promotes a reversible discoverability cue.
baseline_decision: BUILD: add a permanently visible recovery/settings entry or tooltip whenever a plugin hides standard menu items so users are never dependent on an undiscoverable Option+Click gesture.

evidence: Post-freeze issue search found reports involving hideDisablePlugin and shortcut/menu behavior, including issue #438, but those establish implementation inconsistency in a neighboring path rather than whether users discover Option+Click.
No admissible repository/issue evidence found in this adjudication establishes noticeability or comprehension of the hidden-control recovery gesture; that exact claim remains FIELD-owned.
adjudication.decision_delta: Neta prevented a discoverability redesign that the baseline recommended without R6 evidence. The issue corpus contains neighboring implementation bugs but does not close the perception claim.
adjudication.lesson: A documented recovery gesture and its implementation can be established at R1 while its discoverability remains an R6 question. HOLDOUT result is score-only until the holdout wave closes.
